newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold demand in limbo, awaits April pickup.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold demand in limbo, awaits April pickup.

text.p: Demand for gold in Dubai has lost its shine after a strong run early this year, but traders expect business to pick up by April with the start of a month-long gold promotion and stronger buying from a neighbouring country.
"The retail market is a little slow. Everyone is waiting to buy during the Shopping Festival so they can have a chance to win one kg in the daily draw," said a trader.
"Pakistan is also slow," added the trader, who is in re-export business to the Indian subcontinent.
Dubai is hosting a shopping promotion from March 27, when shop-owners hope to lure big customers with a chance to win up to 41 kg of gold in raffle draws over a month.
They said the outlook for sales to Saudi Arabia was good, particularly with the haj pilgrimage of some two million Moslems to Islamic holy sites in the kingdom beginning in mid-April.
"With haj in 20 to 25 days' time, people are already starting to manufacture jewellery for export to Saudi Arabia," one said.
"Many pilgrims like to take home a gold memento. It's like people visiting the Vatican like to bring home a picture of the Pope, pilgrims who go on haj like some memento," he said.
Dubai traders say big sellers during haj are pendants in the shape of the Kaaba, the large cubic stone structure which stands in the the Grand Mosque of Mecca, and necklaces on which to hang them.

While local and Saudi demand is expected to pick up during the next month, Dubai's traders say that business is likely to start slowing down to the Indian subcontinent -- the emirate's key re-export destination -- as summer nears.
"Every year from about April to June trade to India and Pakistan slows down," said one trader.
Others said more gold had recently been moving successfully to Pakistan though illegal channels, avoiding customs duties.
In February, when world gold prices fell sharply, gold imports into Dubai -- mostly for re-export -- more than doubled to a record 56.05 tonnes from 23.48 tonnes in February 1996.

Releasing the figure, a fresh monthly record after the previous high of 46.35 tonnes in January, World Gold Council regional chief executive Rolf Schneebeli said: "The entire region is buying gold. India is buoyant and Pakistan is slowly returning to its old gold buying habits."
Low world gold prices in February boosted demand, which has since died down as prices have moved up to around $350 an ounce, traders say.
On Sunday, traders quoted the Dubai benchmark Ten Tola (TT) bar at around 4,875 dirhams ($1,328), little changed from the level on March 16. The TT bar is 3.746 ounces of 24-carat gold.
On the international market, bullion was last quoted on Saturday at $352.65/353.15 an ounce from $352.25/75 a week earlier.
